sectionHeadings: 112: Typed overlays ride the existing seam
3.1 An overlay is declared frontmatter, and nothing else
3.2 The engine reads an overlay's shape and never its meaning
3.3 The consumer owns the meaning, and says so
3.4 Overlays coexist by namespacing, not by luck
3.5 What an overlay establishes, and what it does not
3.6 Attaching to a unit, which is the one thing the seam does badly
record.summary: Four proposals (effect contracts, budgets, dependency rationale, contract adapters) all want to attach typed data to a unit without changing what a unit is. The corpus already has the seam for that: declared extra frontmatter, preserved verbatim into the registry. This states the contract an overlay keeps so four of them can coexist without any of them reaching the engine. Deferred: specified now, built when a consumer names the need.
record.title: Typed overlays ride the existing seam
